solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of collection's a breach-loading weapon

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old firearm collection includes a gun loaded at the breech, though 'breach' is spelt to mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' signals letters sitting inside the phrase: collectionS A BREach. The odd spelling 'breach' is needed for the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a curved cavalry sword, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Dismiss society hack wasting hours

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the hours letter drops out of hack

parts.note: taken as the word hack

explanation.surface: A society gossip writer is fired for idling away their working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to fire them from their job.

clue.text: Runs in to catch crow

indicators.note: in says the runs letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: to bag something is to catch or capture it, as a hunter does
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone rushes in to grab a crow, the black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like the bird but is the verb to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, which is what bragging means.

clue.text: Train and inspire to hope getting time for clubs

indicators.note: getting introduces the letter brought in as a replacement
for means in place of, so time stands in for clubs

parts.note: to encourage someone is to give them hope and confidence
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A coach describes training and motivating a team, with time spent on golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting time for clubs' swaps the C in ENCOURAGE for a T. 'Train' is a noun here, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is the line of attendants following an important person, which is an entourage.

clue.text: Unexpected danger parking the thing before autumn

parts.note: P is the standard map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
IT is a pronoun standing for the thing
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A warning about the hazards of leaving your car somewhere before autumn arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn, which non-American solvers may need to think of.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden trap or hazard that catches people unawares.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about one copyright infringer

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the numeral

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly and at length
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone babbles nonsense about a person who breaks copyright law.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate copies and sells material illegally, breaching the owner's copyright.

clue.text: Couple starting to work out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are rearranged, as in put out of order
starting to work means just the opening letter of work

explanation.surface: A pair of people beginning to exercise at the gym together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes W from work; with TO that gives TOW, and 'out' mixes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, so two of something.

clue.text: Sufficient nowadays to regard as equal

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of dates, so it means nowadays
to equate things is to treat them as equal

explanation.surface: These days it is enough to treat everyone the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is enough for the purpose, merely sufficient.

clue.text: Tough lay there quivering

indicators.note: quivering means shaking, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tough lay there trembling, perhaps after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery meat or skin is hard and tough like leather.

clue.text: Preach movingly about Lot's end in part of Genesis?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
movingly suggests the letters of preach are shifted into a new order
Lot's end points to the final letter of the name Lot

explanation.surface: A preacher delivers an emotional sermon on the fate of Lot, whose story is told in Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movingly' turns PREACH into CHAPER, and 'about' puts T (Lot's end) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is a book of the Bible divided into numbered chapters; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Time after Post Office returned major work?

indicators.note: after places the time piece behind the other piece
returned means the letters for Post Office are written backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spends time after a postal job on a big project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PO into OP, which is followed by ERA. Opus is Latin for work, and an opera is a large musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a large-scale staged musical composition, hence a major work; the question mark flags the wordplay on opus.

clue.text: Small pig hearts tough to pierce with a blade

parts.note: a runt is the smallest, weakest piglet of a litter
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
rough can mean tough or hard, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: A grim picture of butchering a little pig whose hearts are tough to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through is to stab them right through with a sword or similar blade.

clue.text: Perhaps Windrush side split over right place to keep money

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the next in this down entry

parts.note: to rive is an old word meaning to split or tear apart
a bank is where money is kept

explanation.surface: A Windrush-era account of a dispute over the right place to deposit money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Windrush is a river in the Cotswolds of England, though the surface evokes the Windrush generation of Caribbean migrants.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windrush is a river, so its edge is one example of a riverbank, as 'Perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Semolina made by US company in company with us

parts.note: taken as written
CO again stands for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American firm produces a semolina dish in partnership with our own.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are CO and US, twice over: 'US company' and 'company with us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African food made from small steamed granules of semolina.

clue.text: Go off having assignation outside school

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps around the school

parts.note: an assignation is a romantic meeting, a date
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil goes absent to keep a secret romantic rendezvous beyond the school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is a famous English private boarding school. 'Go off' reads as leaving, but is the explosive sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that goes off explodes, which is to detonate.

clue.text: United approach is never coming back

definitions.note: describes the answer as a phrase, standing for the adjective one-way

parts.note: people who are united are as one
an approach or method is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A football fan laments that Manchester United's style of play has gone for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way ticket takes you out with no return journey, so its holder is never coming back.

clue.text: On-screen icon gave data card, but no peripherals

indicators.note: having no peripherals means each of the three words loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Computer-speak: a user handed over a data card for a picture, peripherals not included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no peripherals' strips the first and last letter of each word: AV, AT, AR. 'Peripherals' looks like computer kit, fitting the on-screen theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the small picture or figure that represents a user on a screen or in a game.

clue.text: Agree to swindle scoundrel

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
cur is an old word for a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone consents to cheat a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, to agree.

clue.text: Son gutted about swine making a display at match

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: an apple that is cored has had its insides taken out, so gutted
a boar is a male pig, a swine

explanation.surface: A boy upset over a pig shows his feelings at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son gutted' tempts a reading of an empty S...N, but gutted is CORED, which goes 'about' BOAR to give COREBOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard is the large board displaying the running score at a sports match.

clue.text: Beer? Mine's got nitrogen in

indicators.note: in says the element goes inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine; the 's stands for has
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts that their beer is nitrogen-infused, like a smooth stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine's' reads as 'my drink is' but is the noun mine, a PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a standard measure in which beer is served, so beer by example, as the question mark shows.

clue.text: Refuse 500 yen for working

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: working means the letters are set in motion and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone turns down five hundred yen in pay for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny someone something is to refuse it to them.

clue.text: Old judge to make a speech

parts.note: to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: An elderly judge prepares to address the court.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, often pompously.

clue.text: Dine on steak, say, but not medium

indicators.note: but not means the medium letter is left out

parts.note: steak is an example of meat
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone eating steak, but wanting it cooked anything other than medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' looks like a steak cooking order but is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a meal.

clue.text: Girl's after church goblet

indicators.note: after puts the girl's name behind the church letters

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A young woman follows the church service to receive the communion cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large drinking cup, especially the one used for wine at Communion.

clue.text: Lieutenant in utter retreat

indicators.note: in says the officer's letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: sheer means utter or absolute, as in sheer nonsense
Lt is the military abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An army officer is caught up in a total rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reads as a military withdrawal in the surface but is the noun for a place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a safe place to withdraw to, just as a retreat is a refuge.

clue.text: Catherine earmarked money for cat

definitions.meaning: A pet form of the name Catherine
a pool of money put aside for a shared purpose
an affectionate word for a cat

explanation.surface: Catherine set aside some funds to buy a pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a nickname, a communal fund, and a pet word for a feline.
